utterance: Hi Samuel, I'm the doctor looking after you. Tell me about the pain—where did it start, where is it now, and has it changed since last night?
reply: It started around my belly button about ten o'clock last night, so maybe fourteen hours ago, and it moved down to the right sometime overnight. At first it sort of came and went, but it is there all the time now, and I would say it is about a seven out of ten.

awards.label: Whether the pain is constant or comes and goes
Red flag: Where the pain started and whether it has moved

utterance: Does walking, coughing or moving make it worse? Have you felt sick or vomited, and did that start before or after the pain? Have you had a fever or chills?
reply: Yeah, walking hurts, every bump in the car on the way here was awful, and coughing is the worst. I have felt sick since the early hours and threw up once this morning, but the pain came first and the sickness came a few hours later. I also felt hot and a bit shivery last night.

awards.label: Red flag: Whether moving, walking or coughing makes it worse
Whether the pain or the vomiting came first
Red flag: Fever, sweats or chills

utterance: Have you had any appetite, and when did you last eat or drink? Any diarrhoea, constipation, blood in your poo, or difficulty passing wind? Any burning or blood when you wee, pain in your back, or pain or swelling in your testicles?
reply: I couldn't face breakfast and am not hungry at all, which isn't like me, though I just had the usual food from mum's cooking on Sunday. I haven't had any diarrhoea, just went normally yesterday morning and nothing since, and definitely no blood. Weeing is completely normal, and there's nothing wrong down there.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Pain or swelling in the testicles

utterance: Have you ever had pain like this, any operations, or any other medical problems? Have you taken any medicines or painkillers, and do you have any allergies? Also, what time did you last have anything to eat or drink?
reply: I have never had anything like this before, and I've never had an operation, so I've still got my appendix as far as I know. I took a couple of paracetamol at six this morning, but it didn't do much.

awards.label: Whether he has had this pain before

utterance: The pattern of your pain makes me concerned about appendicitis, which is inflammation of a small pouch attached to the bowel. I'll gently examine your tummy now. Is that okay? To check before treatment, do you have any medicine allergies, and when did you last eat or drink?
reply: I had a bit of mum's cooking on Sunday, but I haven't eaten since, and I don't have any medicine allergies. Go ahead.

finding: Flat. No scars. Moves little with breathing.
Right lower quadrant: Marked tenderness, maximal at McBurney's point, with voluntary guarding. Central (periumbilical): Mild tenderness only. Elsewhere: soft and non-tender.
Right lower quadrant: Tender to light percussion. Elsewhere: resonant and non-tender.

utterance: You are very tender over the appendix, with signs that the lining inside your tummy is irritated. You need urgent assessment in hospital by the surgical team today; this isn't something to watch at home. I'd also like to briefly check your testicles, with a chaperone, because problems there can sometimes cause tummy pain. Is that okay?
reply: Really? Do I have to go to hospital right now? Can't it wait until tomorrow?

utterance: Yes, you need to go now. An inflamed appendix can burst and cause a serious infection; waiting until tomorrow would be unsafe. The hospital can give fluids and pain relief, do blood tests and a scan if needed, and decide whether you need an operation. Please don't eat or drink while we're arranging this, as you may need an anaesthetic. Are you happy for the brief testicle examination?
reply: Alright, let's just get it done.

finding: Both testes normal lie, non-tender, no swelling.
Both testes normal lie, non-tender, no swelling.

utterance: I'll arrange an ambulance so you can be monitored and have pain relief on the way, and I'll call the emergency team. Before giving a small dose of strong pain relief, have you used any alcohol, sleeping tablets or other drugs today, and do you have any breathing problems?
reply: I had a few beers on the weekend, but nothing this week. I haven't noticed anything like that with my breathing.

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment
Phone the emergency department with a handover

result: Leucocytes trace, nitrites negative, blood trace, protein negative, ketones +.

dose: 2.5 mg by slow intravenous injection; monitor breathing, oxygen saturation and blood pressure

utterance: The ambulance and hospital assessment are being arranged. My working diagnosis is appendicitis; a leak or burst appendix needs to be ruled out urgently. I'll hand over the timing of your pain, examination findings, temperature and the pain relief given. We'll keep you here lying comfortably and monitor you until the ambulance arrives. Please tell us straight away if the pain spreads or suddenly changes, you feel faint, or you have trouble breathing. Don't drive yourself. Is there someone you'd like us to contact for you?

awards.label: Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Perforated viscus with peritonitis
